chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abdullah ibn Muskan, from whom he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The blood money (diyah) of a fetus, before the soul is breathed into it, is one hundred dinars. When the soul is breathed into it, its blood money is one thousand dinars or ten thousand dirhams. If it is male, [the amount is as stated]; and if it is female, [the amount is] five hundred dinars. And if a woman is killed while pregnant and it is not known whether it is a male or a female, the blood money for the child is half: half the blood money of the male and half the blood money of the female, and her [own] blood money is complete.

key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: A silver coin, used here as a unit of currency
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: A gold coin, used here as a unit of currency
key_terms.دِيَةُ: Blood money or financial compensation for injury or death

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money (diyah) for a fetus in Shia Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar establishes the foundational jurisprudence of fetal compensation, distinguishing between the pre-soul (nutfah) stage and the post-soul (ruh) stage, with specific monetary values for male and female fetuses. It further addresses the legal ambiguity of an unknown fetal sex by mandating a combined partial payment, reflecting the Shia scholarly approach to equitable financial restitution in cases of uncertainty.
